Show search and charts. This build contacts public APIs for Apple Podcasts search (itunes.apple.com), Apple charts (rss.marketingtools.apple.com), fyyd.de and gpodder.net. Those requests carry no credentials and no user identifiers.

Video links (optional). Paste a video page link or a BV ID into the search field and that video is played as an episode: the app asks the video site\'s public API (api.bilibili.com) for the title, cover and audio address, then streams from its content delivery network (*.bilivideo.com and similar) and caches the audio locally like any other episode. The requests do not sign in and carry no user identifiers; to obtain the audio address they are sent with a browser User-Agent and the video site\'s referring page, so the site sees those and your IP address. Episodes from video links cannot be downloaded; their automatic cache is cleared together with everything else by \"Clear cache\".

Reverb processes most data on your device. It has no developer backend, account, ads, analytics, attribution, third-party login or push, crash reporting, or cross-app tracking. Subscriptions, history, favorites, downloads, playback cache, listening statistics, settings, a random installation ID, and runtime logs are processed locally and are not automatically uploaded to the developer. Android uses open-source foundations such as AndroidX, OkHttp, and Coil, but no SDKs for those reporting purposes. Since 1.0.2, if backup is enabled in system settings (Android cloud backup or vendor device migration), the operating system copies subscriptions, favorites, history, download records (links only), stamps, notes, listening statistics, and settings to your own system cloud account or new device; audio, transcript and chart caches, and logs are not included, and the switch lives in system settings.

When online, search terms, region, or category are sent to public directories such as Apple, fyyd, and gpodder. RSS, artwork, audio, and transcripts are requested directly from publishers or hosts, which exposes your IP address, User-Agent, and requested resource to them. Logs may contain show or episode identifiers and the host names of accessed services; they leave the app only when you choose to share or export them. Read the full policy for details.

Tapping "Agree and continue" means you have read and accept this policy.

Reverb is a lightweight podcast client with an ink-and-wash aesthetic. Discover shows, subscribe, download for offline, and resume anytime — focused on listening.

· Discover: browse daily charts by region and category; reorder and swipe between categories
· Search: by name or paste an RSS URL
· Video links: paste a Bilibili video link or BV ID and listen to it as an episode (no sign-in; episodes from video links cannot be downloaded)
· Share shows: create an image with the show artwork, title and Reverb branding
· Radio: roam at random or follow time-of-day moods
· Updates: every episode from the shows you follow, newest first, on its own tab
· Library: six shelves — subscriptions, up next, favorites, downloads, history, notes
· Batch and shortcuts: tap an episode cover to open its channel; in Updates, Favorites, Downloads, History or a channel page, long-press a row and pick "Select multiple" to add the whole batch to Up next
· Offline downloads: keep downloaded episodes on this device, Wi-Fi-only optional
· Playback cache: episodes you play stay on this device and replay offline; loaded lists and artwork stay browsable without a connection, clearable in Settings
· Transcript: transcribe on device, or read the publisher's own transcript
· Playback: speed, skip, sleep timer, play modes (sequential / repeat one / shuffle), resume, background & lock-screen controls
· Notes: mark the second a line lands on you and write a word about it; the Notes shelf turns them into a timeline you can tap back into
· Show notes: swipe on the player
· New-episode notifications
· In-app updates: download the new version on device and hand it to the system installer (asks first when you are not on Wi-Fi)
· System backup: subscriptions, favorites, history, download records (links only), stamps, notes, listening stats and settings are backed up by the OS and migrate with device changes; audio and transcripts are not included
· Appearance: dark/light/system, text size, accent color, multiple languages

Visually it draws on ink, celadon and beam-gold — the name and icon echo “an echo circling the rafters.”

For sources it stays entirely free, no login, no API key: discovery relies on public sources, and it always returns to the publisher’s own RSS and streams the original audio — copyright-clean, zero cost.

For privacy, subscriptions, history and downloads stay on your device, are not automatically uploaded to the developer, and are not used for cross-app tracking.

Offline speech-to-text. This build bundles offline speech recognition (the open-source whisper.cpp plus a bundled model). Turning an episode\'s audio into text happens entirely on your device — the audio is never uploaded, never leaves the device, and never passes through any server. You can turn this off in Settings.
Light up each word as it is spoken. On-device recognition produces word timings along the way, so this costs no extra transcription time.

Real spectrum (optional). Turning on "Real spectrum" in Settings makes the ink wave follow the actual loudness. That needs microphone access, which the system asks for separately when you enable it; the audio is only analysed on device — never recorded, stored or sent anywhere — and is no longer used once you turn the switch off.

In-app updates (optional). On launch this build asks GitHub\'s public releases endpoint (api.github.com) which version is the latest. The request carries only this app\'s own public repository address and its current version number — never an account, an identifier, your subscriptions or what you listen to. It downloads only when that answer really has a newer version, and by default only over Wi-Fi; on a metered network it asks first and starts if you agree. The system installer then takes over — this app never installs anything itself — and the "Install unknown apps" permission that step needs is requested by the system only when you choose to install.
